model.name: lebowski
model.notes: 877M ConvNeXt encoder, host-kept history, no RL residual. Checkpoint 6f5c8d09/ecc73f48. The model the G55 runs.

public_open_loop.condition: Measured. comma's public two-camera segments (openpilot CI data), native intrinsics and the device's own calibration, both cameras; every model on the same decoded frames. Truth is what the recording car did next: carState speed and acceleration, yaw rate from the device's cameraOdometry. Segments where the car never moves have no data. 39 of the 45 listed segments have a score, from 23 drives and 20 cars.

public_closed_loop.condition: Measured. comma's worldmodel-4B generates each next frame at 5 Hz from 9 history frames, 5 recorded anchor frames and the car's pose; the model drives comma's ideal car (the requested curvature and acceleration happen at once) for 7.2 s from the recorded start. Distance is to the recording car's own path. One window per segment, nearest the middle, where the car holds at least 5 m/s for the window and the 4.8 s before it; segments with no such stretch are left out. Seeds 0 and 1, averaged per segment. 28 of the 45 listed segments have a score, from 19 drives and 17 cars.

The truck closed loop with a disturbance while the model drives; only the tests listed ran. 2° off heading: an extra 2°/s yaw for the first second. 18 windows (9 day, 9 night). 0.5 m off centre: an extra yaw-rate pulse, out and back over the first 2 s, that would move an uncorrected car 0.5 m sideways with no net heading change. 18 windows (9 day, 9 night).

limits: Open-loop scores compare a model's action with what the recording driver or car did; a model that drives differently but well is scored as wrong, and smoother, later actions (what comma's RL residual produces by design) score worse here. Measured on the 2026-10-27 deep dive: open-loop accuracy did not predict closed-loop driving.

Closed-loop numbers come from a generative world model, not a car. Nothing separates models before about 2 s; past about 4 s the recorded anchor frames pull every model back toward the recorded path, so 4 s is the primary horizon.

Intervals are 95% percentile bootstraps that resample whole drives (the drive a public segment was cut from, the recorded drive a truck window comes from), so segments of one drive count once. Below 10 drives there is no interval: the truck sections come from fewer drives and report means and win counts only.
Paired deltas are model minus baseline on the units both have (for lateral gain, the change in its distance from 1); wins count units where the model is better in the metric's direction.

Lateral best-correlating lag is searched from 0 to 1.5 s; a lag at either edge is censored and left out. Plan speed error at 3 s reads the plan head, which does not separate models built on one frozen base: it is identical on every segment for the four f22e06e5 models, and for Cinque v2 and v3.
Truck open loop pools few windows (camera mounts changed between drives); read it as a check that a model works on the truck's camera, not a ranking.
Truck closed loop: the steering and powertrain simulation is fitted to the G55, not validated on it in closed loop; the reference is the driver's own line, not the lane centre.

Recovery tests are disturbances rendered by the world model (yaw it renders; a one-frame jump it does not, so none is used). The braking-lead test is not built yet: the drives the truck closed loop can use hold no window where a car ahead brakes.
